meanings.note: Possession, relationships and many fixed expressions.
Tener algo claro means to understand it or have a firm view of it.

examples.text: Tiene muy claro lo que quiere.
examples.trans: She is very clear about what she wants.
She has a lot of talent.
Thank you very much for everything.
What do we have? We have lots of things.

meanings.note: Más de introduces a numerical threshold; keep the written accent.

examples.text: Lleva más de un año aquí.
examples.trans: She has been here for more than a year.

meanings.note: Auxiliary before a past participle; does not express possession.
The impersonal present is hay, not ha.

examples.trans: How did she do that by email?
You know this suit by heart.
Tonight we're going to the cinema.
Can you check that socket for me?

meanings.note: Links a clause after a judgment in the first lesson example; introduces a relative clause about people in the second.

examples.trans: I'm looking for people who work here.

examples.text: Hay que abrir un poco la óptica.
examples.trans: We need to broaden our perspective a little.

meanings.note: In poco a poco, the two occurrences belong to one expression meaning gradually.

examples.trans: Little by little, I'm understanding it.

examples.text: Hay que abrir un poco la óptica.
examples.trans: We need to broaden our perspective a little.

meanings.note: Identity, profession or a characteristic; compare estar for a state or location.
Unstressed direct object; can refer to a statement or idea rather than a masculine physical object.
With a gerund, presents an action developing over time.

examples.text: Poco a poco hemos ido mejorando.

meanings.note: Marks many specific human direct objects without a separate English word; in poco a poco it belongs to the expression little by little.

examples.text: Igual aquí hay una joya por descubrir.
examples.trans: Maybe there is a gem to discover here.

meanings.note: Contact someone or call out to them.
The reflexive form llamarse gives a name.

examples.text: A veces también lo llaman para protagonizar.
examples.trans: Sometimes they also call him for a leading role.

meanings.note: In farewell expressions, introduces the next meeting; do not translate the farewell word for word.

examples.trans: I'll call you tomorrow without fail.
